redRegression.before: 6000-round eight-player rules were admitted and persisted. The new test expected rejection and failed before the service used create admission.
redRegression.after: Rejected before publishing match or selection; original roster is unchanged.

boundDerivation: Each roster player has one action; a claim targets at most one tile, with at most one contest and one resolution event per target. Their combined maximum encoding also exceeds a pass event.
Two teams each emit at most one spending and one regeneration event. A settlement event is conservatively counted every round.
Use largest field encodings admitted by the fixed v1/v2 engines: 32 ASCII team characters, 127 coordinates, int maximum counters, final-round tick and maximum evidence sequence.
Reserve the envelope, every possible pending action and all 128 observer UUIDs. Multiply the serialized frame bound, plus separator, by the unchanged published duration.
At new-game admission, sum active final bounds and completed history sizes plus 8192 bytes for viewer/input headroom. Existing oversized legacy games reserve the full 8 MiB cap.
coverage: Maximum engine duration generates a 16 MiB JSON replay even with only pass actions; streaming counter avoids retaining a duplicate JSON tree.
Legal contested rounds, regeneration, settlement, pending actions and all observers remain within the derived bound.
Default 1200-round four/eight-player matches are admitted, over-bound duration and duplicate creation are rejected.
Catalog reserves future active-game growth after restart; completed game restores identical final state and frees room for a new match.
Legacy v1 oversized-duration replay remains readable and savable without commitment or schema changes.
limitations: The conservative bound may reject durations whose particular action sequence would fit; it admits enough room for all legal sequences in the fixed engine.
Legacy games already admitted without this check can still reach the unchanged actual file cap; they are not silently truncated or migrated.
Preflight does not reserve physical disk space or protect against outside file modifications. Atomic saves still report I/O failure and preserve prior data.
No new live-server, human, fairness or production performance evidence. Timings under constrained JVM memory are not capacity measurements.
Ephemeral signer self-tests do not constitute a formal release signature. Full P0-P11 objective remains active.
